note.note:
ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 2-day history of lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain; no specific trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Constant mid-suprapubic discomfort for ~48 h. Feels intermittently “hot and sweaty.” Mild nausea without vomiting. Pink-tinged urine noted once. Mild increase in urinary frequency. Constipated last week, now normal bowel habit.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change/hoarseness, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No similar episodes; no prior urinary infections reported. No previous hospital visits for this issue.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Amoxicillin (reaction details not documented).
  • Current medications: None regularly. No over-the-counter meds. Prior contraceptive implant removed 1 y ago.
- Social context: Lives with parents; non-smoker; drinks ~1 beer 4×/week. Consultation conducted privately.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No respiratory complaints; no stridor or breathing difficulty noted.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (only self-reported home temperature 37 °C).
- Presence of another person: Not specified to be present during call.

Assessment:
Working clinical impression: Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower urinary tract infection).
Evidence summary: Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, visible hematuria, minimal systemic features, no flank pain.
DDx (aligned with transcript):
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – high likelihood; classic symptom triad present.
2. Urolithiasis – medium likelihood; hematuria and abdominal pain compatible but pain not colicky and frequency more suggestive of infection.
3. Early appendicitis – low-medium likelihood; central pain and mild systemic symptoms, but urinary findings argue against.  
No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Prescription: 3-day oral antibiotic course (twice daily) sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy; start immediately upon collection.
- Advice: Maintain adequate hydration. Monitor symptoms closely.
- Escalation / red-flag instructions: Seek urgent review if pain worsens, develops high fever/chills, back/flank pain, worsening hematuria, vomiting, or any breathing/airway difficulty (none currently but counselled).
- Follow-up: Contact service if no improvement after antibiotics, recurrence of symptoms, or development of new symptoms. Consider face-to-face examination and urinalysis/culture if no response.
- Preventive / educational measures: Encourage regular fluid intake, complete antibiotic course, avoid unnecessary irritants (e.g., perfumed hygiene products). No ENT-specific interventions required at this time.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected: Objective vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂), physical abdominal and ENT examination, urine dipstick/culture, pregnancy test, details of amoxicillin reaction, documentation of prior anaphylaxis plan or auto-injector (if relevant to allergy).  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None.  
● Transcript quality: Clear conversation; minor pauses but content intelligible.
